en: So to do that, I opened my terminal here,
the one integrated into Visual Studio Code,
which is just the program I'm using for
viewing this folder. You can open up your
regular terminal or PowerShell outside of
any editor too.
Just make sure that you navigate into this
project folder and then run npm install to
install the dependencies of this project,
the
n8n
package, for example, which we'll use. You
can ignore any warnings you may be getting
here. And once that finished without an
error, again, warnings are fine, you can run
npm start to start a local server which
serves an n8n instance.
And you must keep that process running as
long as you plan on working on that workflow
visually. And you can always shut it down
and restart it once you're ready to get back
into it. You do shut it down by pressing
Ctrl+C.
And then again, with npm start again in this
project, you restart it.
Now you'll see when that starts, it should
offer you to press O to open it in the
browser, or you copy whichever address you
see here and open that in a browser
manually.
And if you do so, you should see a sign up
or a sign in form.
Sign up if you did never sign in before,
sign in if you did sign in before, which I
did. And even though this is running
locally, you need to create an account. You
can enter whatever data you want though. You
just need to remember the email and password
you chose so that you can sign back in the
future.
And once you did that, once you created an
account and signed in,
you are inside of n8n and ready to dive into
creating and managing workflows with it.
